ap_microeconomics-f02.title: A perfectly competitive firm and its market

stimulus.description: Total cost of producing cotton for a typical firm in a perfectly competitive, constant-cost cotton industry.

notes: The market for cotton is currently in long-run equilibrium at a price of $28 per ton.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw correctly labeled side-by-side graphs for the market for cotton and for a typical firm, both in long-run equilibrium at a price of $28 per ton. On your graphs, label the market equilibrium price and quantity ($28 and Q_M), the firm's quantity (Q_F), and the firm's MC and ATC curves.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Market graph: downward-sloping demand and upward-sloping supply meeting at $28 and Q_M. Firm graph: U-shaped ATC with MC crossing it at its minimum, a horizontal price line at $28, and Q_F where the price line meets MC.

required_elements: Draws downward-sloping demand and upward-sloping supply curves with Price and Quantity labeled on the axes and the intersection labeled with the price and Q_M
alt_solutions: labels may be written as P and Q or as price and quantity
curves may be labeled D and S or demand and supply
common_errors: omits axis labels
draws both curves with the same slope sign
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Draws U-shaped MC and ATC curves on the firm graph, with MC crossing ATC at the minimum of ATC and a horizontal price line at the long-run price touching ATC at its minimum
alt_solutions: the price line may be labeled as demand, marginal revenue, or price
MC may be drawn as a rising curve through the minimum of ATC
common_errors: draws ATC as a downward-sloping line only
places the price line above or below the minimum of ATC
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Labels the firm's quantity Q_F where the price line meets MC and shows the same price on both graphs
alt_solutions: Q_F may be marked on the horizontal axis directly below the MC-price intersection
the firm quantity is labeled at the minimum of ATC
common_errors: labels Q_F at the minimum of MC
uses different prices on the two graphs
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Suppose market demand for cotton increases and the market price rises to $32 per ton. Using the table, calculate the firm's profit-maximizing quantity and its economic profit at that price.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Marginal cost of the 6th ton is $31, below $32, and the next ton costs $33, above it, so the firm produces 6 tons. Profit = $32 x 6 - $172 = $20.

required_elements: Finds the last ton whose marginal cost does not exceed the price (the quantity answer is correct)
alt_solutions: price equals marginal cost
compares each additional ton's cost with the price
common_errors: uses the quantity that minimizes average total cost
uses the largest quantity in the table
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Computes total revenue minus total cost at the profit-maximizing quantity (the profit answer is correct)
alt_solutions: price minus ATC times quantity
total revenue less the table's total cost
common_errors: forgets to subtract total cost
uses marginal cost instead of total cost
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: On your graphs from part (A), show the short-run effect of the increase in demand: label the new market price ($32) on the market graph and, on the firm graph, label the firm's new quantity (Q_F2) and shade the firm's economic profit.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Market demand shifts right and the equilibrium price rises to the new price. On the firm graph the new horizontal price line meets MC at Q_F2, and the rectangle between the price and ATC up to Q_F2 is shaded.

required_elements: Shifts the market demand curve to the right and labels the new, higher equilibrium price on the market graph
alt_solutions: draws the new demand curve and labels it D2
shows an arrow indicating the rightward shift
common_errors: shifts the supply curve instead of demand
shows the price falling
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Draws the higher price line on the firm graph, labels Q_F2 where it meets MC, and shades the profit rectangle between the price and ATC up to Q_F2
alt_solutions: shading may be a rectangle outlined and hatched
Q_F2 may be marked on the horizontal axis
common_errors: shades the area between price and MC
labels Q_F2 at the minimum of ATC
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Explain what happens to the number of firms in the industry in the long run and why.
parts.model_answer: ALTON reference answer for self-review — not official AP scoring. Firms are earning positive economic profit, so new firms enter; entry shifts market supply to the right, which lowers the price until economic profit returns to zero.

required_elements: States that firms enter the industry because existing firms are earning positive economic profit
alt_solutions: new firms are attracted by profits
the number of firms increases because price exceeds average total cost
common_errors: says firms exit
says the number of firms does not change in a competitive market
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

required_elements: Explains that entry shifts market supply to the right, which lowers the price until economic profit falls to zero

says price keeps rising
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: E
